title: Örnek test · Rooftop farming
source: Kelime uygulaması için yazılmış özgün örnek metin

parts.title: Part 1
parts.passage_subtitle: Can rooftop agriculture feed tomorrow's cities?

passage.label: A
passage.text: Over the past two decades, rooftops in many of the world's largest cities have begun to change colour. Where there was once grey concrete and gravel, there are now beds of lettuce, rows of tomatoes and even small orchards. Rooftop farming, once a hobby for a handful of enthusiasts, has become a serious business in places such as New York, Singapore and Montreal.

passage.label: B
passage.text: The appeal is partly practical. Cities contain vast areas of flat roof that receive direct sunlight for most of the day, yet are rarely used. Growing food close to where it is eaten also reduces the distance it must travel, and many urban farms deliver their produce to restaurants on the same morning it is harvested.

passage.label: C
passage.text: There are environmental arguments too. A layer of soil and plants absorbs rainwater that would otherwise flood drainage systems during storms. Researchers in Toronto found that a planted roof held back up to 60 per cent of the rain that fell on it during a typical summer. Green roofs also keep the buildings beneath them cooler, lowering the demand for air conditioning.

passage.label: D
passage.text: However, the challenges are considerable. Most older buildings were not designed to carry the weight of wet soil, and strengthening a roof can cost more than the farm will earn in several years. Access is another problem: staff, tools and harvested crops must all be carried up and down, often in lifts shared with office workers.

passage.label: E
passage.text: To reduce weight, many growers have turned to hydroponics, a method in which plants grow in nutrient-rich water rather than soil. Hydroponic systems can be up to ten times lighter than traditional beds, and they use less water because it is recycled. Critics point out, though, that they depend on electricity for pumps and lighting.

passage.label: F
passage.text: The economics remain uncertain. A study of 30 commercial rooftop farms in North America found that only a third were profitable without grants or donations. Those that succeeded tended to grow high-value crops such as herbs and microgreens, or to earn additional income from educational tours and private events.

passage.label: G
passage.text: Supporters argue that profit is not the only measure of success. Rooftop farms, they say, reconnect city residents with the origins of their food and create green spaces in neighbourhoods that have few parks. Whether these benefits justify public funding is a question many city councils are now being asked to answer.
